_note: Every dataset, paper and page Hygieia relies on. UI numbers that claim to be real link to /sources#<id>. `fetched_at` is filled in by `npm run fetch-data` for sources that have a snapshot in data/snapshots/.

sources.title: Measurements of Energetic Particle Radiation in Transit to Mars on the Mars Science Laboratory
sources.used_for: Transit profile: mean daily dose equivalent inside a spacecraft on the way to Mars (the paper reports 1.84 ± 0.33 mSv/day).
sources.credit: Zeitlin et al., Science 340, 1080 (2013). MSL RAD: NASA/JPL-Caltech/SwRI.

sources.title: Mars' Surface Radiation Environment Measured with the Mars Science Laboratory's Curiosity Rover
sources.used_for: Mars surface profile: mean daily dose equivalent in Gale Crater over the first ~300 days (the SwRI/NASA release quotes 0.67 mSv/day; the paper gives 0.64 ± 0.12).
sources.credit: Hassler et al., Science 343, 1244797 (2014). MSL RAD: NASA/JPL-Caltech/SwRI.

sources.title: First measurements of the radiation dose on the lunar surface
sources.used_for: Lunar base profile: daily dose equivalent on the lunar surface (1369 µSv/day), about 2.6 times the dose inside the ISS.
sources.credit: Zhang et al., Science Advances 6, eaaz1334 (2020). Chang'E 4 Lunar Lander Neutrons and Dosimetry (LND).

sources.title: DOSIS & DOSIS 3D: radiation measurements with the DOSTEL instruments onboard the Columbus Laboratory of the ISS in the years 2009–2016
sources.used_for: Station profile: daily dose equivalent in low Earth orbit. 0.575 mSv/day is a demo midpoint between two published anchors: this paper reports up to 0.647 mSv/day in Columbus (end of May 2016), and the Chang'E 4 paper puts the lunar rate at about 2.6 times the ISS rate (about 0.53 mSv/day).
sources.credit: Berger et al., J. Space Weather Space Clim. 7, A8 (2017). ESA DOSIS / DOSIS 3D, DLR.

sources.title: ESA HREDA — DOSIS: Dose Distribution inside the ISS
sources.used_for: Linked as the open archive record of the DOSIS experiment in Columbus. Not downloaded by the demo.
sources.credit: ESA Human and Robotic Exploration Data Archive (HREDA).

sources.title: ESA Human and Robotic Exploration Data Archive (HREDA)
sources.used_for: Reference archive for ESA human-spaceflight experiments. Linked only.

sources.title: Monitoring radiation for astronaut health
sources.used_for: Neutron channel of the personal dosimeter: CSA states neutrons contribute about 30% of total radiation on the ISS. Hygieia applies the same share to dose in the other profiles as a demo value. The dosimeter is modelled on CSA's CANS instrument.

sources.title: Why do we conduct science experiments in space?
sources.used_for: Background for the Earth-impact pitch (About page). Linked only.

sources.title: DONKI — Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information
sources.used_for: Real solar energetic particle events (SEP) and solar flares (FLR) from the last 365 days, replayed on the mission clock. Snapshot: data/snapshots/donki.json.

sources.title: GOES integral proton flux (primary satellite, 7 days)
sources.used_for: Current S-level on the Space Weather panel. NOAA S-scale: S1 = 10, S2 = 100, S3 = 1 000, S4 = 10 000, S5 = 100 000 pfu of ≥10 MeV protons. Snapshot: data/snapshots/goes_protons.json.

sources.title: NOAA Space Weather Scales — Solar Radiation Storms
sources.used_for: Definition of the S1–S5 solar radiation storm levels.

sources.title: NASA OSDR Biological Data API
sources.used_for: Study metadata (title, OSD id, organism) for the "Evidence in NASA OSDR" links in the knowledge base. Metadata only, no raw omics. Snapshot: data/snapshots/osdr_studies.json.

sources.title: NASA OSDR RadLab — multi-agency space radiation dosimetry
sources.used_for: Linked as the place to explore real ISS dosimeter time series. Linked only: the demo does not download a series from it, so none is plotted.

sources.title: NASA OSDR Environmental Data Application (EDA)
sources.used_for: Real ISS cabin telemetry. Linked only: the demo does not download a series from it, so Hygieia's cabin samples are synthetic and labelled demo values.

sources.title: 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight
sources.used_for: Framework for the feature map on the About page: space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, gravity fields, hostile/closed environments.

sources.title: Human Research Program — Risks
sources.used_for: The 17 risks listed on the About page and in the knowledge base. A caption on the page calls the eye syndrome now known as SANS (there under its older name, VIIP) NASA's leading spaceflight-related health risk.

sources.title: Ongoing HRP Research
sources.used_for: Models for the simulated sensors and logs: ARCHeR (well-being, activity and sleep monitoring on Artemis II), Standard Measures (same core set for every astronaut), Zero T2 (exercise without a treadmill). Thigh Cuff and B-Complex are described only as studies under investigation.

sources.title: Counteracting Bone and Muscle Loss in Microgravity
sources.used_for: Exercise prescription in microgravity profiles (120 min/day): NASA reports station crews exercise an average of two hours a day.

sources.title: NASA OCHMO Technical Brief: Carbon Dioxide (NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 2, V2 6004)
sources.used_for: Amber line for cabin CO₂: NASA-STD-3001 limits the average one-hour CO₂ partial pressure to no more than 3 mmHg. The red line (6 mmHg) is a demo value.
sources.credit: NASA Office of the Chief Health and Medical Officer.

sources.title: Worst-case one-way Earth-Mars light time
sources.used_for: Transit and Mars profiles: maximum one-way communication delay. The value is the maximum of the real Earth-Mars light time over one full cycle, computed by JPL Horizons (snapshot: data/snapshots/light_time.json) and rounded down to whole minutes. The demo compresses it to 20 seconds.

sources.title: One-way Earth–Moon light time
sources.used_for: Lunar base profile: one-way communication delay, the mean Earth-Moon light time from JPL Horizons (snapshot: data/snapshots/light_time.json).

sources.title: JAXA PADLES — passive dosimetry in the Kibo module
sources.used_for: Independent ISS area-dosimetry record a real system could cross-check the Station dose rate against. Linked only.

sources.title: JAXA DARTS — SEDA-AP space environment data (Kibo exposed facility)
sources.used_for: Radiation and plasma data from outside the ISS (2009–2018); a candidate second source for the space-weather replay. Linked only.

sources.title: DLR MARE — Matroshka AstroRad Radiation Experiment on Artemis I
sources.used_for: Beyond-low-Earth-orbit dose measurements with body phantoms; motivates Hygieia's per-crew dose tracking. Linked only.

sources.title: INPE EMBRACE — Brazilian Space Weather Program
sources.used_for: Brazil's space-weather monitoring programme and weekly briefings; a candidate regional source for the Space Weather panel. Linked only.

sources.title: Demo values
sources.used_for: Everything labelled "demo value": recovery response coefficients, most clinical thresholds (SpO₂ and temperature hard limits, cabin pressure, temperature, noise and light ranges), partial-gravity exercise prescriptions, the size of the dose spike during a replayed solar particle event, the 6 mmHg CO₂ red line, and the mission plan durations. Not medically validated.

sources.title: JPL Horizons ephemeris service
sources.used_for: Real Earth-Mars and Earth-Moon distance and one-way light time for each mission day: the link-delay card and the Houston console show the real delay for today. Snapshot: data/snapshots/light_time.json.

sources.title: Planetary K index
sources.used_for: Geomagnetic activity on the Space Weather page. NOAA G-scale: G1 starts at Kp 5. Relevant in low Earth orbit (Station profile). Snapshot: data/snapshots/kp_index.json.

sources.title: NASA POWER - Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources
sources.used_for: Earth mode (Remote clinic profile): daily maximum air temperature and relative humidity at the demo clinic site, turned into an outdoor heat index. Snapshot: data/snapshots/power_heat.json.
sources.credit: NASA Langley Research Center POWER Project.

sources.title: Heat Index equation and safety categories
sources.used_for: Earth mode: the Rothfusz heat-index regression and the NWS categories (Caution from 80 F, Extreme Caution from 90 F, Danger from 103 F, Extreme Danger from 125 F) used on the outdoor heat card.
sources.credit: NOAA National Weather Service (U.S. public domain).

sources.title: Sources and effects of ionizing radiation - average natural background dose
sources.used_for: Earth mode (Remote clinic profile): the dose rate, the world-average natural background of 2.4 mSv per year (0.0066 mSv/day), for comparison with the space profiles.
sources.credit: United Nations Scientific Committee on the Effects of Atomic Radiation, 2008 report.

sources.title: Canadian Space Agency open data portal
sources.used_for: A place to look for Canadian ISS dosimetry data. Nothing from it is used: the neutron share comes from the CSA article. Linked only.
sources.credit: Canadian Space Agency, Open Government Licence - Canada.

sources.title: WHO guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour
sources.used_for: Earth mode (Remote clinic profile): the activity target. WHO advises adults to do at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity activity a week; Hygieia reads that as 30 minutes a day.
